articles.title: Hudbay Delivers Record Third Quarter 2026 Results, Further Improves Cost Guidance and Advances Copper Growth Pipeline
articles.description: TORONTO, Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Hudbay Minerals Inc. ("Hudbay” or the "Company”) (TSX, NYSE: HBM) released its third quarter 2026 financial results today. All amounts are in U.S. dollars, unless otherwise noted. "Hudbay delivered record performance this quarter, with revenue of $766 million achieving a new record and adjusted EBITDAi of $413 million resulting in record trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of $1.5 billion, and we are well on our way to delivering the 12th consecutive year of achieving annual consolidated copper production guidance and the 6th consecutive year of achieving annual consolidated gold production guidance,” said Peter Kukielski, Chief Executive Officer. "The strength of our diversified operating platform and the dedication of our people helped to achieve a new record for mill throughput at Constancia, significant increases in mine productivity at Lalor, record mill throughput at New Britannia and record gold recoveries at Stall during the third quarter. Our three-year operational turnaround at Copper Mountain has delivered the first quarter of positive free cash flowi since our acquisition. We are extremely well positioned to continue to prudently reinvest in several high-return growth opportunities across the business to further enhance our exposure to copper and gold. Following the quarter, Hudbay and Mitsubishi achieved a significant milestone with the final investment decision at Copper World, one of the best copper growth projects in the Americas, offering some of the highest copper grades, lowest cash costs and favourable capital intensity. We continue to solidify our position as a premier Americas-focused copper producer with a pipeline of long-life, low-cost assets in tier-one jurisdictions.” "Our diversified operations in Canada and Peru continued to achieve strong copper and gold production, with operating efficiencies, which have more than offset external cost pressures and allowed us to improve our 2026 full-year consolidated cash cost guidance for a second time this year and also improve our 2026 full-year sustaining cash cost guidance,” said Eugene Lei, President and Chief Financial Officer. "We generated over $200 million in free cash flow during this quarter and more than $400 million year-to-date, even after investing over $325 million in sustaining capital across our operations. Our strong free cash flow generation and balance sheet strength position us well to fund our share of the Copper World project and make generational investments in our operating mines to double our copper production per share. This is consistent with our disciplined capital allocation framework, which focuses on generating the highest risk-adjusted returns while advancing our industry-leading growth pipeline.” Delivered Record Third Quarter Results; Production Guidance Reaffirmed and Cost Guidance Further Improved Achieved record quarterly revenue of $765.9 million, net earnings attributable to ownersi of $149.5 million, and quarterly adjusted EBITDAi of $413.4 million, driven by steady operating performance, attractive operating margins and strong exposure to copper and gold across Hudbay's diversified operating portfolio. Higher consolidated copper production of 30,152 tonnes and gold production of 69,513 ounces in the third quarter of 2026, representing a 7% and 36% increase, respectively, compared to the second quarter of 2026. Continued to demonstrate industry-leading margins with consolidated cash costi and sustaining cash costi, net of by-product credits, of $(0.19) and $1.61 per pound of copper, respectively, in the third quarter of 2026. Reaffirmed full year 2026 consolidated production guidance including 110,000 to 138,000 tonnes of copper and 217,000 to 272,000 ounces of gold. Further improved full year 2026 consolidated cash costi guidance range to $(0.55) to $(0.35) per pound of copper, an additional improvement from the previously updated guidance range of $(0.45) to $(0.25) per pound of copper, as year-to-date results are trending well below the low end of the cash cost range. Improved full year 2026 consolidated sustaining cash cost guidance range to $1.40 to $1.80 per pound of copper from the original guidance range of $1.70 to $2.10 per pound of copper as a result of strong exposure to gold by-product credits and continued strong operating cost control. Full year 2026 consolidated sustaining capital expenditures expected to be $35 million lower than guidance levels due to lower capitalized stripping in Peru and British Columbia and capital deferrals and efficiencies. Peru operations demonstrated steady operating performance with production of 20,572 tonnes of copper and 5,267 ounces of gold in the third quarter of 2026. Peru cash costi, net of by-product credits, of $2.23 per pound exceeded the upper end of the 2026 annual guidance range of $1.70 to $2.10 per pound primarily due to lower by-product credits, partially offset by better treatment and refining charges. Achieved record Constancia mill throughput of approximately 91,000 tonnes per day in the third quarter, on track to achieve 34 million tonnes per annum in 2027. Manitoba operations demonstrated strong operating performance and executed on the commitment to deliver a stronger second half of 2026 with production of 57,261 ounces of gold, 3,012 tonnes of copper, 3,691 tonnes of zinc and 268,346 ounces of silver in the third quarter of 2026. Manitoba cash costi of $403 per ounce of gold outperformed the low end of the 2026 annual guidance range of $500 to $800 per ounce as a result of higher by-product prices. Continued to exceed Snow Lake mill performance expectations with record New Britannia mill throughput of 2,250 tonnes per day and record Stall gold recoveries of 73.6% in the third quarter. British Columbia operations showed improving operating performance with production of 6,568 tonnes of copper, 6,985 ounces of gold and 52,010 ounces of silver in the third quarter of 2026, in line with quarterly cadence expectations. British Columbia cash costi of $3.09 per pound of copper was higher than the annual cost guidance range of $1.50 to $2.50 per pound primarily due to elevated fuel prices, higher fuel consumption from increased material moved and timing of equipment maintenance. While British Columbia cash cost is expected to improve in the fourth quarter with higher expected production volumes, full year cash cost is expected to track towards the high end of the annual guidance range. Achieved Copper Mountain mill throughput of approximately 43,500 tonnes per day in September, reflecting successive monthly increases after the completion of mill maintenance at the primary SAG mill in July, and on track to achieve the targeted 50,000 tonnes per day by the end of the year. The third quarter represented the first quarter of positive free cash flowi at Copper Mountain since its acquisition by Hudbay, demonstrating the benefits from continued operating efficiencies, recent mill improvement initiatives and ongoing execution of the accelerated stripping program. Third quarter earnings per share attributable to owners was $0.34, reflecting strong gross profit margins as a result of the continued focus on cost control and higher metal prices more than offsetting higher input costs. After adjusting for various non-cash items on a pre-tax basis, third quarter adjusted earningsi per share attributable to owners was $0.34. Cash and cash equivalents were $788.7 million and total liquidityii was $964.3 million at the end of the third quarter of 2026, before giving effect to a $250 million increase in size to Hudbay’s credit facilities in November 2026. Cash and cash equivalents exclude $50.1 million in U.S. municipal bond proceeds that are classified as restricted cash and reflect $45.0 million in net purchases of investments and $22.0 million of debt repayments during the third quarter of 2026. Record Trailing Twelve-Month EBITDA and Free Cash Flow Generation; Strong Balance Sheet and Significant Financial FlexibilityHudbay's unique copper and gold diversification across its operations, together with a focus on cost control across the business, continues to realize strong margins and generate significant free cash flow. Operating cash flow before changes in non-cash working capital was $313.9 million during the third quarter of 2026, reflecting an increase of $103.8 million compared to the second quarter as a result of record quarterly revenue and maintaining strong operating margins. Delivered free cash flowi generation of $201.9 million during the third quarter of 2026, reflecting an increase of approximately $100 million compared to the second quarter through higher production and continued strong operating margins. Generated more than $400 million of free cash flow year-to-date in 2026 despite investing over $325 million of sustaining capital in the business over this period. This has resulted in record trailing twelve-month free cash flow generation of $631.0 million. Achieved quarterly adjusted EBITDAi of $413.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, resulting in record trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDAi of $1,542.4 million. Recorded net debti of negative $0.1 million as at September 30, 2026, positioning the Company well to reinvest in high-return growth capital projects across the business, including the recently announced final investment decision ("FID”) to proceed with the development and construction of Copper World. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratioi was 0.0x in the third quarter of 2026, significantly improved from 0.4x in the fourth quarter of 2025 as a result of the initial proceeds received from Mitsubishi Corporation ("Mitsubishi”) on closing of the Copper World joint venture transaction in January 2026, along with strong cash flows from operations. Consistent with Hudbay’s prudent balance sheet management and balanced capital allocation framework, Hudbay repaid $22.0 million of its outstanding $272 million draw on its revolving credit facilities in the third quarter of 2026. As announced with the Copper World FID in October, Hudbay proactively amended and extended its existing revolving credit facilities. Total capacity under the facilities was upsized from $450 million to $700 million and the maturity date of the facilities was extended by two years to November 2030. The amended credit agreements include an improved pricing grid and greater financial flexibility that reflects Hudbay’s robust cash flow, strong balance sheet position, and its recently upgraded credit rating. After adjusting for the $250 million increase in size of the credit facilities, Hudbay’s proforma liquidity as of September 30, 2026 is approximately $1.2 billion. Advancing Brownfield and Greenfield Investments to Drive Strong Returns and Significant Production GrowthFormally approved, along with Mitsubishi, the FID to proceed with the construction and development of Copper World as the next major copper mine in the U.S. with first production targeted for the second half of 2029. The FID is supported by robust economic returns with low capital intensity outlined in the Copper World definitive feasibility study and related pre-feasibility studies (collectively, the "DFS”) which delivers annual copper production of 102,000 tonnes over the first 10 years, an 11% increase when compared to 92,000 tonnes in Hudbay’s 2023 pre-feasibility study for Copper World ("2023 PFS”). The base case for Copper World contemplates a 15-year mine life utilizing mineral reserves and requires only state and local permits ("Base Case”) and expands the concentrator in year five to enable a 43% increase in average annual copper production to 120,000 tonnes in years six to 10 compared to 84,000 tonnes over the first five years. The Base Case generates an after-tax net present value (8%) of $1.2 billion and internal rate of return of 17% at a long-term copper price of $5.00 per pound, which increases to $2.3 billion and 22%, respectively, at a copper price of $6.00 per pound. The extension case for Copper World contemplates a 37-year mine life utilizing only measured and indicated mineral resources and expands mining activities onto federal lands in year 10, subject to obtaining federal permits ("Extension Case”), maintaining annual copper production of 117,000 tonnes from years 11 to 20. The Extension Case generates an after-tax net present value (8%) of $2.5 billion and internal rate of return of 19% at a long-term copper price of $5.00 per pound, increasing to $4.0 billion and 24%, respectively, at a copper price of $6.00 per pound. As a result of Hudbay’s capital allocation strategy and prudent Copper World funding plan, the levered internal rate of return to Hudbay increases to 32% at $5.00 per pound of copper long-term in the Base Case and to 44% at $6.00 per pound of copper in the Extension Case. Enhanced the gold production profile at Snow Lake and extended reserve mine life to 18 years with updated life of mine plan released in September. Total life-of-mine gold production increased by 60% and reserve mine life extended by an additional two years to 2043, which together with the four-year extension in March 2026 represents a total of six years added to the reserve mine life. Updated five-year averageiii annual gold production of 185,000 ounces reflects continued strong mill throughput rates at New Britannia and higher gold recoveries at Stall, representing a 37% increase in total gold production from an additional 250,000 ounces produced over the same five-year period in the Snow Lake 2021 technical report. Snow Lake updated mineral reserve estimates increased contained gold to 2.0 million ounces, and the updated mine plan represents a conservative view based on Hudbay’s historical high resource-to-reserve conversion rate of 90%iv and ongoing exploration activities. There remains 1.5 million ounces of gold contained in inferred mineral resource estimates. Implementing mill enhancements at Constancia to drive further increases in mill throughput and copper recoveries. The completion of the installation of a third rougher line late in the third quarter is expected to drive higher copper recoveries starting in the fourth quarter. The installation of two pebble crushers is nearing completion with commissioning expected in November, resulting in increased processing capacity at the Constancia mill. Advancing the development of infrastructure at the New Ingerbelle extension project in British Columbia and de-risking the path to first production in late 2028. New Ingerbelle is expected to enhance the copper and gold production profile and secure a longer mine life at Copper Mountain. Advancing the recently acquired Cactus project in Arizona by initiating pre-feasibility study ("PFS”) activities, including multiple trade-off studies, with completion expected in the second half of 2027. Continuing to derisk the long-term Mason project in Nevada through PFS and other site activities. The Mason PFS is expected to be completed in the second half of 2027. Positive Exploration Results Across the BusinessRecent exploration drilling in Peru intersected a potential new high-grade feeder system at Constancia in multiple drill holes, with highlights including 245 metres of 0.43% copper and 0.03% molybdenum, indicating high-grade expansion potential beneath and adjacent to the existing reserve and resource envelope. Follow up drilling is underway. Continuing to execute an extensive exploration program in Snow Lake from recently developed underground exploration drifts at Lalor and 1901 to enable infill drilling and testing of mineralized extensions, while also testing identified high-priority targets at the former producing New Britannia gold mine currently on care and maintenance (the "Britannia Gold Project”). Regional geophysics, mapping, structural modeling and data compilations underway to support target definition for new anchor deposits. Completing a targeted drilling program at New Ingerbelle focused on upgrading existing inferred resources to reserves to further optimize and extend the mine life at Copper Mountain. Results are expected to be incorporated in Hudbay’s annual reserve and resource update in March 2027. Summary of Third Quarter Results Hudbay's diversified asset portfolio delivered consolidated copper production of 30,152 tonnes and consolidated gold production of 69,513 ounces in the third quarter of 2026, positioning the Company well to meet full-year 2026 consolidated production guidance. Consolidated copper production was higher than the second quarter of 2026 as a result of record high mill throughput in Peru and higher grades offsetting lower mill throughput in British Columbia. Consolidated gold production was higher than in the second quarter of 2026 primarily due to increased throughput and grades in Manitoba. Consolidated silver production of 897,587 ounces was higher than the second quarter of 2026 primarily driven by increased mill throughput and higher grades, while zinc production of 3,691 tonnes in the third quarter of 2026 decreased compared to the second quarter of 2026, primarily reflecting lower zinc grades at the Manitoba operations. Cash generated from operating activities was $214.9 million during the third quarter of 2026, reflecting a decrease of $82.1 million compared to the second quarter of 2026, primarily driven by unfavourable changes in non-cash working capital. Operating cash flow before changes in non-cash working capital was $313.9 million during the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $103.8 million compared to the second quarter of 2026, primarily reflecting higher realized copper prices and increased sales volumes. Adjusted EBITDAi was $413.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, a 29% increase compared to $321.2 million in the second quarter of 2026, primarily due to higher realized copper prices and higher copper, gold and silver sales volumes. Net earnings attributable to owners was $149.5 million, or $0.34 per share, in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $137.4 million, or $0.34 per share, in the second quarter of 2026. The strength in aggregate earnings resulted from the aforementioned high revenue due to higher sales volumes of all metals, and cost control resilience in the face of higher diesel prices. Adjusted net earnings attributable to ownersi and adjusted net earnings per share attributable to ownersi in the third quarter of 2026 were $149.5 million and $0.34 per share, respectively, after adjusting for various non-cash items on a pre-tax basis including $13.4 million in evaluation expenses, a $5.4 million mark-to-market revaluation net loss on various financial instruments, share-based compensation and offsetting mark-to-market gains on investments, a non-cash $11.8 million gain in re-evaluation adjustment on environmental provisions, among other items. This compares to adjusted net earnings attributable to ownersi and net earnings per share attributable to ownersi of $113.5 million and $0.28 per share, respectively, in the second quarter of 2026. The increase is a result of higher realized metal prices for copper and zinc and the aforementioned higher sales volumes. Consolidated cash costi, net of by-product credits, in the third quarter of 2026 was $(0.19) per pound of copper, compared to $(0.40) per pound in the second quarter of 2026. The increase from the second quarter of 2026 was in line with the expected cost cadence and is the result of lower by-product credits and slightly higher mine operating costs. Consolidated sustaining cash costi, net of by-product credits, in the third quarter of 2026 was $1.61 per pound of copper, compared to $1.39 per pound in the second quarter of 2026. This increase was primarily due to the same factors impacting consolidated cash cost noted above. Consolidated all-in sustaining cash costi, net of by-product credits, in the third quarter of 2026 was $2.25 per pound of copper, higher than the second quarter of 2026 due to the same reasons noted above. As at September 30, 2026, total liquidityii was $964.3 million, including $788.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, which excludes $50.1 million in U.S. municipal bond proceeds that are classified as restricted cash, and undrawn availability of $175.6 million under Hudbay's revolving credit facilities (prior to giving effect to the $250 million increase in size to the credit facilities in November 2026). Cash and cash equivalents reflect $45.0 million in net purchases of investments and $22.0 million in debt repayments during the third quarter of 2026. Net debti at the end of the third quarter was negative $0.1 million. Hudbay expects that its current liquidity, together with cash flows from operations, will be sufficient to meet the Company's liquidity needs for the next 12 months. With the successful execution of its disciplined capital allocation strategy, attracting Mitsubishi as a long-term strategic joint venture partner and a prudent project funding plan, Hudbay’s Copper World capital contributions are expected to be approximately $500 million, representing less than 25% of the initial growth capital, with capital contributions not expected to be required until 2028. articles.title: 93% of paint splatters are valid Perl programs!
articles.description: The Entropy of Syntax: An Analysis of Perl's Lexical Permissiveness The proposition that 93% of random paint splatters constitute valid Perl programs is a provocative study in the intersection of computability, language design, and extreme syntactic flexibility. This claim, originating from a presentation at SIGBOVIK 2019, challenges traditional notions of how programming languages delimit their valid lexical space. By examining the underlying grammar of Perl 5, we can determine why such an apparently chaotic assertion possesses a foundation in the language’s unique approach to parsing and execution. Lexical Foundations and the "Anything Goes" Philosophy At its core, Perl 5 is built upon a philosophy of TMTOWTDI ("There's More Than One Way To Do It"). Unlike languages that strictly enforce structured indentation or rigid grammatical constructs, Perl’s lexical analyzer is designed to be highly forgiving. The Perl 5 parser, historically implemented as a massive, hand-written recursive descent parser (a "Yacc-gone-wild" architecture), allows for significant ambiguity. The primary mechanism that drives the high success rate of arbitrary character sequences as valid code is Perl’s treatment of identifiers, symbols, and expressions. In many languages, an unexpected character triggers an immediate syntax error. In Perl, the interpreter attempts to resolve almost any string of tokens into a tree of opcodes, provided the baseline requirements for script completion—namely, balancing blocks and quotes—are satisfied. Quantifying Validity: The Stochastic Probability Model To test the 93% claim, one must define the bounds of the "paint splatter." If we assume a paint splatter can be modeled as a sequence of bytes, the question becomes: how many of these sequences are valid Perl source files? The validity of a program in Perl 5 is governed by its ability to pass the compilation phase. This phase requires that: The lexer can tokenize the stream. The parser can construct a valid Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). The program concludes with a valid sequence of tokens. The reason for the high validity percentage lies in the "implied" nature of Perl. Consider the following: # A standard "empty" Perl script 1; This is valid. Furthermore: # This is also valid 'a'; And even: # Valid as well { 'a' } When we introduce random noise, the probability that the noise happens to form a structure that Perl can interpret as a "noop" or a bareword expression is statistically significant. Because Perl treats a bareword (an unquoted string) as a string literal or a function call depending on the context, and because it allows the last expression of a block to serve as the return value, the "surface area" for a valid script is vast. Code Analysis: The Mechanics of Chaos To demonstrate why random noise often results in valid Perl, consider the following script designed to approximate the "splatter" logic: #!/usr/bin/perl use strict; use warnings; # Function to generate random noise sub generate_splatter { my $len = shift; my @chars = ('a'..'z', 'A'..'Z', '0'..'9', ' ', ';', '{', '}', '"', "'"); return join('', map { $chars[rand @chars] } 1..$len); # The validation cycle sub is_valid { my $code = shift; # Capture stderr to suppress compilation errors open(my $fh, '>', '/dev/null'); open(local *STDERR, '>&', $fh); # Attempt compilation without execution return eval "sub { $code }; 1"; When iterating over random strings, the parser frequently encounters sequences that satisfy the grammar. If the generated string contains balanced braces and semicolons, Perl interprets the intermediate segments as scalar expressions. In Perl, 1; is a valid statement. Therefore, if a splatter contains a 1 and a ;, the probability of it being valid increases significantly. As the input length increases, the probability of validity fluctuates, but the "looseness" of the lexer ensures that the parser remains remarkably resilient to malformed input. The Role of Pragmas and Deprecation The reason this behavior is not viewed as a catastrophic failure of the language is that Perl 5 was never intended to be a strictly typed, pedantic environment. It was designed for text processing. In a world where one is manipulating messy, unformatted logs, a parser that throws a fatal error on a trailing comma or an undefined bareword is an impediment. However, this flexibility is a double-edged sword. As modern Perl (Perl 5.30+) has evolved, the inclusion of use strict; and use warnings; has become the standard. These pragmas intentionally restrict the permissive nature of the language. If the 93% claim were tested against a codebase forced to use use strict;, the percentage would plummet toward zero. The "splatter" validity is a feature of legacy Perl—the "bare" Perl that lacks the guardrails modern developers now require. Comparative Syntax Analysis When comparing Perl to other languages such as C, Java, or Rust, the contrast is stark. A Rust compiler, for instance, requires strict adherence to memory safety, type checking, and ownership rules. A random byte sequence in Rust will almost certainly fail at the lexing or borrow-checking stage. Perl, by contrast, operates on a "best effort" basis. In the parsing stage: Identifier tokens are loosely defined. Statement boundaries are inferred via semicolons or block ends. Expression evaluation is deferred or optimized in ways that allow malformed (but technically valid) syntax to pass initial compilation. This creates a "syntax-heavy" environment where the language is essentially a massive set of heuristics for converting arbitrary input into executable opcodes. Implications for Language Design The study of this phenomenon highlights a critical trade-off in language design: the balance between expressiveness and safety. Perl’s design prioritizes expressiveness and the reduction of developer friction, which manifests as an extremely permissive grammar. While this allows for "clever" code and rapid prototyping, it also allows for the "splatter" phenomenon—where randomness is indistinguishable from intention. Modern language design has largely moved toward the "principle of least surprise." Developers now prefer languages where syntax errors provide clear, actionable feedback rather than languages that attempt to interpret noise as intent. The Perl experience remains a landmark study in what happens when the parser is optimized for "don't crash," rather than "don't accept invalid logic." Conclusion: The Limits of Interpretation The 93% figure should be interpreted as a metric of the language’s lexical tolerance rather than a measure of its computational utility. It demonstrates that the Perl grammar is so broad that it can encapsulate almost any arbitrary grouping of symbols into a syntactically valid (if semantically nonsensical) structure. While this allows Perl to parse highly fragmented and unstructured data, it highlights the technical debt inherent in allowing the parser to bridge the gap between randomness and execution. For organizations navigating complex system architectures, legacy code migrations, or the implementation of robust software development lifecycles, understanding the underlying behavior of languages like Perl is essential. Complex systems demand precision, and while flexibility is a tool, it must be governed by rigorous engineering standards to prevent the sort of ambiguity that allows "paint splatters" to be treated as legitimate instruction.
